facts.summary: The preliminary report identifies auditable human-AI workflows and explicit criteria for escalation to human oversight as governance requirements. Its short-, medium- and long-term trajectories are possible futures rather than completed developments.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment containing prospective scenarios, July 2026.

facts.quote:
These gains are real but 
conditional: they depend on local contextualization, 
adequate infrastructure, and human preparation.
facts.summary: The preliminary report links benefits in science, health, education and agriculture to local context, infrastructure and human preparation, identifying teacher readiness and digital capacity gaps as barriers to equitable deployment.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of sectoral capacity needs.

facts.quote:
Agricultural AI systems are most sustainable 
when treated as shared public infrastructure 
with clear governance
facts.summary: The report frames agricultural AI as shared public infrastructure and states that sustained anticipatory food-security impact depends on embedding solutions in national institutions and accounting for smallholder conditions.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of institutional conditions for agricultural AI.

facts.quote:
The evidence base is biased toward advanced 
economies, large firms and formal work.
facts.summary: The report cautions that economic findings concentrated in advanced economies and formal digital work may not generalize to developing economies. Productivity gains require complementary investments in data, skills and organizational change.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment; evidence limitation rather than a universal economic forecast.

facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of measurement capacity needs.
